content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price increases, then correct downward — model fails to capture this lagged correction.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially in the 10–20 day window, suggesting underweighting of downward volatility or overconfidence in recent trends.
- Model fails to adjust for mean reversion in the final 5–10 days, often holding forecasts too high when true values are trending down.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to over-forecasting in the immediate future when true values are trending lower.
